clue.text: Stylish US city, previously obscured

indicators.note: something obscured is hidden from view, so this word is blotted out of the city's name

parts.note: Chicago is the big city in Illinois
previously means ago, as in 'long ago'

explanation.surface: A fashionable American city whose earlier history has been forgotten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'obscured' removes AGO (previously) from CHICAGO.
explanation.definitionFit: Chic is a French-derived synonym for elegant and fashionable.

clue.text: Strong and healthy runner learning limits

indicators.note: limits here is a verb: the learning word bounds the runner on both sides

parts.note: study is learning, as in years of study
R stands for river, the classic crossword runner since rivers run

explanation.surface: A fit athlete whose education has kept them in check.
explanation.walkthrough: 'limits' puts R inside STUDY, between ST and UDY. 'Runner' looks like an athlete, but it is a river, abbreviated R.
explanation.definitionFit: Sturdy describes a robust, solidly built person in good health.

clue.text: Perhaps I eye hemp on Soho trip?

indicators.note: a trip is a drug-fuelled hallucination, so these letters are scrambled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone stoned on cannabis wandering London's Soho district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trip' rearranges HEMPONSOHO. Soho is a nightlife district of central London; 'hemp' and 'trip' set up a drugs picture.
explanation.definitionFit: The words I and eye are an example of pairs pronounced alike but spelt differently.

clue.text: Brilliant Mr Stein's finally taken silk?

parts.note: fab, short for fabulous, means brilliant

indicators.note: the final letter is taken away from the chef's first name

parts.note: Rick Stein is a well-known British TV chef

explanation.surface: Praise for a celebrity chef who has finally become a senior barrister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally taken' removes the K from RICK. Rick Stein is a British TV chef. 'Taken silk' is British slang for becoming a King's Counsel, a senior barrister, but here silk is a cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Silk is one example of a woven material, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Where you might find a bad setter?

definitions.text: Where you might find a bad setter?

parts.words: Where you might find a bad setter?
parts.note: a setter is also a breed of gun dog, and a disobedient dog, or anyone in disgrace, is sent to its kennel

explanation.walkthrough: The setter seems to be the crossword compiler, as if a weak puzzle earned punishment; read it as the dog breed.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog's kennel is where it lives, and being sent there is an idiom for being in disgrace.

clue.text: Good-bye to All That, originally first part of autobiography

indicators.note: originally points to the first letter, how each of these title words begins
the first part of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Good-bye to All That is the title of Robert Graves's memoir, which opens his life story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' takes T, A, T from the title words; 'first part of' adds A from autobiography.
explanation.definitionFit: Ta-ta is a cheery informal British way of saying farewell.

clue.text: Wayward nineties genius

indicators.note: wayward means going astray, so these letters wander into a new order

explanation.surface: A rebellious brainbox of the 1990s.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wayward' rearranges NINETIES.
explanation.definitionFit: The physicist's name has become a byword for a brilliant mind, as in 'he's no Einstein'.

clue.text: Source of water, free from disease

definitions.meaning: a shaft sunk into the ground to draw water

explanation.walkthrough: One word, two senses: a noun for a water shaft and an adjective for being healthy.
explanation.definitionFit: A well is a dug shaft for water, and being well means being in good health.

clue.text: Sensitive matter involving popular King Edward?

parts.note: hot means popular or in demand, as in a hot ticket
King Edward is a popular British variety of potato

explanation.surface: A delicate issue concerning a well-liked British monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: King Edward looks like a monarch but is a British potato variety; 'involving' merely links.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot potato is an idiom for a controversial issue nobody wants to handle.

clue.text: A rebellious modern artist producing cartoon style

indicators.note: rebellious suggests turning over or revolting, so the artist's name is turned back to front

parts.note: Tracey Emin is a contemporary British artist

explanation.surface: A rebel contemporary artist creates work in a cartoon manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rebellious' turns EMIN into NIME.
explanation.definitionFit: Anime is the Japanese style of animated film and television.

clue.text: Motor travel is a kind of cult

parts.note: motor is British slang for a car
to go is to travel

explanation.surface: A claim that driving has become a cult-like obsession.
explanation.walkthrough: A cargo cult is a Melanesian belief that ritual will bring goods from the gods.
explanation.definitionFit: Cargo cult is a fixed phrase for a belief system centred on awaited manufactured goods.

clue.text: Cast her as Lear in early performance

indicators.note: cast suggests throwing or moulding afresh, so these letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A director casts an actress as King Lear in a production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' rearranges HERASLEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A rehearsal is a practice run before the real show.

clue.text: Gypsy chick's accepted, having special powers

indicators.note: accepted means taken in, so the words hold the answer inside them

explanation.surface: A Romany girl is taken in, being supposedly clairvoyant.
explanation.walkthrough: ''s accepted' means the words 'is taken in'; the answer runs across Gypsy chick.
explanation.definitionFit: A psychic claims supernatural abilities such as clairvoyance or telepathy.

clue.text: Plumbing makes a high-pitched noise

definitions.meaning: the system of tubes carrying water in a building

explanation.walkthrough: A noun for tubes and a verb for a shrill call.
explanation.definitionFit: Pipes are the tubes of a plumbing system, and to pipe is to make a shrill sound.

clue.text: Many ignored extremely dumpy adolescent

indicators.note: the extremes, the outer letters, of the word are ignored

parts.note: a teen is an adolescent

explanation.surface: Lots of people paid no attention to a very stout teenager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignored extremely' drops D and Y from dumpy, leaving UMP.
explanation.definitionFit: Umpteen is informal for an indefinitely large number.

clue.text: Toper and moper are miserable together for now

indicators.note: miserable suggests being in a bad state, so these letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A drunkard and a sulker are glum company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'miserable' rearranges TOPERMOPER. A toper is a heavy drinker.
explanation.definitionFit: Pro tempore is Latin meaning temporarily, for the time being.

clue.text: Pole enthralled by Russian Orthodoxy

indicators.note: enthralled means held captive, so the words hold the answer within them

explanation.surface: A Polish person captivated by Russian Orthodox Christianity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' looks like a Polish person but is a point of the earth.
explanation.definitionFit: The North Pole is one of the earth's two geographical poles.

clue.text: Seafood is not evenly pink outside and uncooked in the middle

indicators.note: the selected letters sit on the outside of the next piece
the uncooked word sits in the middle of the chosen letters
the odd letters are taken, not the even-numbered ones

parts.note: raw means uncooked

explanation.surface: A shellfish dish cooked unevenly, pink on the outside and raw within.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not evenly' takes P and N from pink; 'outside' and 'in the middle' put RAW between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A prawn is a small shellfish eaten as seafood.

clue.text: Emollient embrocation and Vaseline initially penetrating inverted part of nipple

indicators.note: penetrating means entering into, so the initials go inside the next piece
an inverted nipple is a real condition, but here the word is turned backwards

parts.note: the areola is the ring of skin round the nipple

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of each word

explanation.surface: Advice on applying soothing ointment to a sore inverted nipple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inverted' turns AREOLA into ALOERA; 'initially' gives E and V, which 'penetrating' puts in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Aloe vera gel is a soothing, softening ointment for the skin.

clue.text: Small leak

definitions.meaning: slang for urinating, as in 'take a leak'

explanation.walkthrough: An adjective meaning tiny and a noun for urination.
explanation.definitionFit: Wee means tiny in Scottish usage, and a wee is a childish word for urination.

clue.text: Keeping back crop when frost is coming is an illegal act

indicators.note: back tells us to read the crop word in the reverse direction

parts.note: the craw is a bird's crop, the pouch in its gullet
rime is hoar frost

explanation.surface: A farmer holding back the harvest when a frost is forecast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keeping back' turns CRAW into WARC. 'Crop' looks like a harvest but is a bird's craw.
explanation.definitionFit: A war crime is an act breaching the laws of armed conflict.

clue.text: Not the first depressing experience for a mistress

indicators.note: the first letter is dropped

parts.note: a downer is a depressing experience

explanation.surface: A depressing experience, and not the first one, for a lover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not the first' removes D from DOWNER. 'Mistress' looks like a lover but means the woman who owns something, as of a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A mistress is a female owner, as in the mistress of the house.

clue.text: Good chap, non-smoker, constrained by bad back

parts.note: S for saint, a good person

indicators.note: constrained by means held inside, so the smoker abbreviation sits in the middle

parts.note: poor means bad, as in poor work
NS is the standard abbreviation for non-smoker in adverts

explanation.surface: A decent chap who does not smoke is held back by a bad back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Good chap' looks like the definition, but it gives S, the saint. 'Back' looks like part of the body, but it is a verb, the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To back a person or venture is to support it, especially financially.

clue.text: Duck into street to get drug in secrecy

indicators.note: into puts the bird inside the street abbreviation

parts.note: the teal is a small duck
H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: Ducking into a side street to buy drugs on the quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duck' looks like a verb meaning dodge, but it is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealth is a quiet, covert way of moving to avoid notice.

clue.text: Lazy and posh, without backbone

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so the backbone wraps the posh letter

parts.note: the spine is the backbone
U means upper-class, posh

explanation.surface: An upper-class idler with no strength of character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but means outside: SPINE goes round U.
explanation.definitionFit: Supine means lying face up, and figuratively passive or lazy.

clue.text: Marriage vow crushed by politician's sex drive

indicators.note: in a down clue, being crushed by means lying under, so the vow comes after

parts.note: Lib is short for a Liberal politician
I do is the vow said at a wedding

explanation.surface: A politician's libido squashes a marriage promise.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'crushed by' puts I DO beneath LIB.
explanation.definitionFit: Libido is the psychological term for sexual desire.

clue.text: Earwig could make part of house fall down

parts.note: the eaves are the overhanging edge of a roof
to drop is to fall

explanation.surface: An insect could bring a bit of the house down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Earwig' looks like the insect but is a British verb meaning to listen in.
explanation.definitionFit: To earwig is British slang for listening secretly to others' talk.

clue.text: Every capital in Europe has a church

indicators.note: a capital letter is the first one of the word

explanation.surface: Every European capital boasts a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital in' takes E, the capital letter of Europe, not a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Each and every both refer to all members of a group individually.

clue.text: Fat girl's fat bottom

parts.note: Sue is a girl's name

indicators.note: in a down clue the bottom of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A rude remark about a plump girl's large behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottom' takes T, the last letter of the second 'fat'.
explanation.definitionFit: Suet is the hard fat from around animal kidneys used in cooking.

clue.text: Maybe Prince of Wales is hip? Only a bit

parts.note: the Prince of Wales is a common British pub name

explanation.surface: A question whether the heir to the throne is trendy, at least partly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prince of Wales' looks like royalty but is a pub sign; 'hip' looks like trendy but is the body part.
explanation.definitionFit: The pubis is one of the bones forming the hip girdle, so only part of it.

clue.text: Tries editing leaders' comments

indicators.note: editing means cutting, here the two leading letters

parts.note: essays means tries or attempts

explanation.surface: An editor tries to rewrite the leader columns' comments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'editing leaders' cuts ES from the start of ESSAYS.
explanation.definitionFit: Says, as a verb, means remarks or comments.

clue.text: Physicist almost wept, having ingested radioactive element

indicators.note: having ingested means having swallowed, so the element goes inside
almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: cried means wept
U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: A scientist nearly in tears after swallowing something radioactive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts CRIED to CRIE; 'having ingested' puts U inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Marie Curie was the physicist who pioneered research on radioactivity.

clue.text: If randy am desperate for male help

indicators.note: desperate suggests wild disorder, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A frustrated man seeks male company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'desperate' rearranges IFRANDYAM. Man Friday is Robinson Crusoe's servant.
explanation.definitionFit: A man Friday is a loyal male assistant, after Crusoe's servant.
